title: Introduce adaptive payload sieves and toolcall windowing in gateway
author: Maya Patel
commit_summary: add adaptive sieving algorithm to stream proxy; introduce per-route payload_sieve config with soft/hard thresholds; implement toolcall windowing to prevent long-lived KV cache stalls; add openai-compat handshake tolerance for fragmented fncall frames; adjust default route weights fallback; add integration tests and docs; feature-flag rollout
description: Motivation: Streaming tool/function-calls in the gateway have been a source of intermittent stalls and head-of-line blocking when large upstream payloads (or fragmented fncall frames from OpenAI-compatible clients) arrive. This PR introduces an adaptive 'payload sieve' in the gateway stream proxy plus a bounded 'toolcall window' for in-flight function/tool writes so that long/large tool outputs cannot block unrelated consumer streams. Summary of changes: 1) Adaptive payload sieve: a lightweight in-proxy filter that observes recent chunk sizes and latency to decide whether to accept, coalesce, or drop/truncate incoming chunks when route-level soft/hard thresholds are exceeded. Configured per-route via route_defaults.yaml and exposed as route.policy.payload_sieve.{soft_limit,hard_limit,coalesce_bytes,drop_policy}. 2) Toolcall windowing: enforce a maximum concurrent writer window per session for fncall/tool output; writers beyond the window are backpressured and, if they exceed a grace TTL, are truncated with a structured failure event so callers can recover. 3) OpenAI compatibility handshake tolerance: tolerate fragmented fncall frames that arrive out-of-order by buffering up to the route's sieve window and signaling a partial-fncall marker to the compatibility layer to avoid infinite stalls. 4) Routing fallback refinements: small change to route selection to prefer lower-latency compatible variants when the sieve detects sustained large-chunk patterns. 5) Tests and docs: added integration test that reproduces prior stall pattern and docs with guidance for operators. Rollout plan: behind feature flag gateway.payload_sieve.enabled (scripts/feature_flags.toml). Start with Canary pool (10% of traffic) for two days, then ramp to 50% if error rates and latency SLOs are stable. Observability: emit metrics gateway.sieve.accepted, gateway.sieve.coalesced, gateway.sieve.dropped, gateway.tool_window.truncated and traces for partial-fncall events. Backwards compatibility: default sieve is conservative (soft limits high) so no behavior change unless flag enabled. Related: ENG-4582 tracks follow-ups to enable dynamic per-tenant limits. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for sieve logic - [x] Integration test reproducing stall - [x] Docs updated - [x] Feature flag + non-default by default - [x] Metrics emitted for monitoring Manual testing notes: run integration-tests/test_stream_toolcalls.py against local gateway with feature flag on, simulate OpenAI fragmented fncall stream using netem to reorder chunks; verify no permanent stalls and that truncated toolcalls produce structured failure event. See commits for details and per-file diffs.
review_thread: Luca: 'Adaptive sieve looks sensible; main risk is accidental truncation—we should ensure structured failure is unambiguous.' Maya: 'Structured failure payload uses code \"SIEVE_TRUNCATED\" and includes original route id and offset for debugging.' Nina: 'Can we make the coalesce window configurable per-tenant later? Logged ENG-4621.' Ethan: 'Integration test is solid; CI flake was a known flakiness in the test harness, reran and it passed.' Approvals: Luca (approved), Nina (approved after small doc tweak), Ethan (approved).
release_notes: Improve gateway streaming stability by introducing an adaptive payload sieve and toolcall windowing to reduce head-of-line blocking and avoid stalls on fragmented fncall frames. Default disabled behind feature flag. Operators should monitor gateway.sieve.* metrics when enabling.
notes_for_ops: When enabling gateway.payload_sieve.enabled, start on Canary with small route soft limits (e.g., soft_limit=512k, hard_limit=4m) and monitor gateway.sieve.dropped and gateway.tool_window.truncated. If truncations spike, increase soft_limit or reduce coalesce_bytes. Alert on sustained increase in gateway.sieve.dropped > 0.5% of requests for a route.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental truncation could affect generator outputs. Mitigation: conservative defaults, structured truncation event for callers to detect and retry, canary rollout and immediate rollback via feature flag. Follow-ups: dynamic per-tenant limits and automated rollback policy (ENG-4621).
